newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle up $1.00 at $70.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle up $1.00 at $70.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets Friday sold $1.00 per cwt higher at $70.00 in brisk trading, feedlot sources said.
About 60,000 head were sold by midday in Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots and by 1500 CDT, USDA confirmed sales on 55,600 in Kansas.
Actual totals for the day will likely be higher because counts lagged during the active day, sources said.
Some packers were short bought and requested Monday delivery of the cattle, a departure from more typical seven-day delivery.

Feedlot cattle prices were underpinned by higher boxed beef prices this week, spurred by this week's lightened holiday slaughter and brisk beef clearance at U.S. supermarkets over the Labor Day weekend, sources said.
USDA estimated the week-to-date slaughter at 596,000 head, well below 711,000 a week ago and 627,000 head a year ago.

Boxed beef prices near midday Friday were quoted up $0.20 to $0.88 per cwt on 139 loads of fabricated cuts reported sold, USDA said. Heavier-weight choice cut prices have jumped $2.69 since last Friday.
